Methods for sdid results

Source: R/sdid.R
sdid-methods.Rd

Standard generics applied to the result of sdid(). weights.sdid() extracts the unit and time weights.

# S3 method for class 'sdid'
print(x, digits = 5, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sdid'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sdid'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sdid'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sdid'
confint(object, parm, level = object$level/100, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sdid'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sdid'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

x, object

The result of sdid().

digits

The number of decimals printed for estimates, standard errors and confidence bounds. Defaults to 5.

...

Passed to sdid_plot() by plot(), and otherwise not used.

parm

Not used, as the result has a single parameter, the effect, named by the treatment column.

level

The confidence level of the interval, as a proportion, such as 0.9. Defaults to the level of the fit.

Value

print()

Prints the header and results tables that sdid() prints, and returns x invisibly.

summary()

Prints the same tables, then for each cohort its number of controls and pre-treatment periods with positive weight and its five largest unit weights, and returns object invisibly.

coef()

The estimated effect, a number named by the treatment column.

vcov()

Its variance, the square of the standard error, as a 1 by 1 matrix whose row and column are named by the treatment column. It is NA without inference.

confint()

A 1 by 2 matrix holding the lower and upper bounds of the normal confidence interval at level, with the row named by the treatment column and the columns by the bounds' percentiles. For a one-sided alternative the interval is one-sided, open in the direction of the alternative.

nobs()

The number of observations, the number of units times the number of periods.

plot()

The trends plot of sdid_plot(), a ggplot object.
